No new leaderboard code is submitted. The strongest complete admissible checkpoint candidate remains the durable RS–RM construction.

Let `p(T)=T^16+T^5+T^3+T^2+1`, `F=F₂[T]/(p)`, and let `α` be the residue class of `T`. Take the explicitly ordered additive subspace `A=span_F₂{1,α,…,α^14}`, of size 32768. Evaluate every polynomial in `F[X]` of degree at most 64 on `A`, obtaining an outer `[32768,65,32704]_{2^16}` Reed–Solomon code. Identify `F` with `F₂^16` in the displayed polynomial basis and encode each symbol by the affine truth table `H(z)_y=z₀+Σ_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`, `y∈F₂^15`. This is the injective binary-linear inner code `RM(1,15)=[32768,16,16384]₂`. Their coordinatewise concatenation is the already-durable `[2^30,1040,535822336]₂` candidate.

The strongest unresolved ordinary-RS route instead requires a presently unavailable deterministic inner `[16384,18,8184]₂`; if supplied, concatenation with `[65536,65,65472]_{2^18}` would give `[2^30,1170,≥535822848]₂`.

Its Krawtchouk coefficients are `f₀=n(2a+2−c)−ca(a+2)`, `f₁=3n−2+a(a+2)−c(2a+2)`, `f₂=2(2a+2−c)`, and `f₃=6`. Whenever these are nonnegative and `f₀>0`, Delsarte gives `A₂(n,d)≤floor(P(n)/f₀)`. At `(n,d,a)=(16384,8183,862)` this is 333941, and at `(16384,8176,496)` it is 593064.

proof_markdown:
### Scope

This is a finite audit of the 24 durable checkpoint submissions and the cited construction templates, not a universal upper bound on binary linear codes.

### 1. The durable 1040-dimensional code

The displayed polynomial `p` passes the degree-16 Rabin test recorded in the durable proof, so `F` has 65536 elements. The evaluation map on degree-at-most-64 polynomials is injective and `F`-linear, hence has binary dimension `65·16=1040`. The affine truth-table encoder is injective and binary-linear. The concatenation is therefore binary-linear, has dimension 1040, and has length `32768·32768=2^30`.

A nonzero outer polynomial has at most 64 roots, so it has at least 32704 nonzero coordinates. Every nonzero `RM(1,15)` word has weight at least 16384. Thus every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least `32704·16384=D`.

For equality, prescribe 64 roots in `A` and form their monic product `g`. Let `u∈F` be the symbol mapped to the constant-one inner word. Among the 65535 nonzero scalars, at most 32704 satisfy `λg(a)=u` at some nonroot `a`. Choose the first remaining scalar in coefficient-vector order. Then all 32704 nonzero inner blocks are balanced, so the resulting word has weight exactly `D`. This independently confirms `[2^30,1040,D]₂`.

### 2. Cubic parity-lattice lemma

For a binary code of length `n` and distance `d`, write `c=n−2d` and `y=n−2x`. Choose `a≡n (mod 2)` and set `P(y)=(y−c)(y+a)(y+a+2)`. At every allowed nonzero distance, `y≤c`; moreover `y+a` is even, so `(y+a)(y+a+2)≥0`. Hence `P(y)≤0`.

Using `K₁=y`, `K₂=(y²−n)/2`, and `K₃=(y³−(3n−2)y)/6`, its Krawtchouk expansion has coefficients

`f₀=n(2a+2−c)−ca(a+2)`,
`f₁=3n−2+a(a+2)−c(2a+2)`,
`f₂=2(2a+2−c)`, and `f₃=6`.

When these are nonnegative and `f₀>0`, the Delsarte inequality gives `A₂(n,d)≤floor(P(n)/f₀)`. Two exact applications are:

- `(n,d,a)=(16384,8183,862)`: `f₀=14578048`, `P(n)=4868214124928`, hence `A₂≤333941<2^19`.
- `(n,d,a)=(16384,8176,496)`: `f₀=7857152`, `P(n)=4659799352320`, hence `A₂≤593064<2^20`.

These bounds apply even to nonlinear codes.

### 3. Exact `2^14` RS-inner ledger

Let the inner code be `[16384,r,d]₂`. A full-length RS outer code over `F_{2^r}` has length `L=65536`, and its maximum usable dimension is `K=L−ceil(D/d)+1`; the binary dimension is `rK`. Alphabet size forces `r≥16`.

- For `r=16`, beating 1040 requires `K≥66`, which forces `d≥8185`. At this distance `K=73`, giving dimension 1168 and distance `D+504`.
- For `r=17`, beating 1040 requires `K≥62`, which forces `d≥8184`. Here `K=65`, giving dimension 1105 and distance `D+512`.
- For `r=18`, beating 1040 requires `K≥58`; again `d≥8184` and `K=65`, giving dimension 1170 and distance `D+512`.
- For `r=19`, the necessary distance is at least 8183, contradicted by `A₂(16384,8183)<2^19`.
- For every `r≥20`, even outer distance 65536 requires inner distance at least `ceil(D/65536)=8176`, contradicted by `A₂(16384,8176)<2^20≤2^r`.

Thus exactly three rank cases survive at this block length.

### 4. Forced residual chain for the nominal `k=1170` gateway

Assume a linear `[16384,18,≥8184]` code exists. If its distance were at least 8185, append an overall parity coordinate. This produces `[16385,18,≥8186]`. With `y=16385−2x`,

`(y−13)(y+1171)(y+1173)=20336856K₀+1392264K₁+4662K₂+6K₃`,

and Delsarte gives fewer than 248153 words, contradicting `2^18`. Its distance must therefore equal 8184. Residualizing a minimum word gives `[8200,17,≥4092]`. If this residual had distance at least 4093, parity extension would give `[8201,17,≥4094]`; the certificate

`(y−13)(y+585)(y+587)=5040824K₀+352760K₁+2318K₂+6K₃`

bounds its size by less than 125418, contradicting `2^17`. Hence the residual distance is exactly 4092, and one more residualization yields `[4108,16,≥2046]`. This narrows the gateway but does not settle existence.

### 5. Remaining ordinary-RS block sizes

Combining the exact Plotkin, shortening, Griesmer, residual, and cubic bounds in the durable `composition-02` and `combinatorial-10` proofs with the lemma above gives the following exhaustive status for full-length, power-of-two-block RS concatenation aimed at dimension above 1040:

| Inner exponent `b` | Status |
|---|---|
| `b≤9` | Closed by alphabet size and Plotkin. |
| `b=10,11,12` | Closed respectively by cardinality bounds `4106<2^13`, `12364<2^14`, and `41537<2^16`. |
| `b=13` | Closed by `A₂(8192,4090)≤116581<2^17` and `A₂(8192,4088)≤151931<2^18`. |
| `b=14` | Exactly the three cases in Section 3 remain. |
| `b=15` | Closed, including the rank-17 and rank-18 exceptional cases proved in the durable submissions. |
| `b=16,17` | Closed by Plotkin plus cubic bounds. |
| `b=18,19` | Closed by shortening and exact cubic certificates, including outer dimensions one and two at `b=19`. |
| `b=20` | Outer dimension at least two is closed; only `[2^20,r,≥523264]`, `1041≤r≤1064`, with outer repetition remains. |
| `21≤b≤29` | Only outer repetition remains; it merely reduces the target to a shorter near-half-distance inner code. |
| `b=30` | Tautologically the original problem. |

Therefore every proper outer-dimension-at-least-two route is closed except the three `b=14` gateways.

### 6. Other audited families

The odd trace-polynomial construction through degree 65 has dimension 991 and character-sum bound `64·2^15=2^21`. Degree 69 would cross 1040 but its generic Weil estimate is too weak. The AGHP powering support forces field exponent at most 15 and degree at most 64, giving core dimension 975; because its homogeneous-Hadamard core has all weights at most `n/2`, adjoining all-one safely corrects this to 976. The exact [Ben-Aroya–Ta-Shma Hermitian specialization](https://www.cs.tau.ac.il/~amnon/Papers/BT.TOC13.pdf) forces `p=64`, divisor degree 512, and Riemann–Roch dimension 37, hence dimension `37·12+1=445` after the same augmentation.

For [Naor–Naor](https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~naor/PAPERS/bias.pdf), a rank-at-least-1041 base has at least 1041 columns. Plotkin forces base relative distance at most one half, while their contraction condition requires at least three independent samples. Thus the Cartesian start already has `1041^3=1128111921>2^30` states. For the literal [HMZ free-walk schedule](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.12606v2), `ℓ=κd^(2κ)r`; if `κ≥2`, then `ℓ≥32` and `d^ℓ≥2^32`, while at `κ=1` their stated bias expression exceeds one. Neither literal construction fits.

The direct Ta-Shma, GUV, Cohen–Cohen, cyclic/BCH, standard Solomon–Stiffler, difference-set, relative-difference-set, and orthogonal-array specializations were likewise eliminated only within the finite hypotheses stated in their durable audits.

Finally, `combinatorial-01` gives a mathematically coherent conditional-expectation calculation at dimension 2971, but its lexicographic bit choice is implemented by exhaustive comparison over all completions. The contribution guide expressly disallows such numerical/exhaustive witness searches. It is therefore not an admissible campaign construction without a new compact structural evaluator.

This proves the scoped audit theorem while leaving the stated inner-code gateways genuinely conditional.

theorem_statement: Scoped checkpoint theorem. At `n=2^30` and `D=535822336`, the durable RS–RM construction is a deterministic binary linear `[n,1040,D]` code. None of the 24 durable submissions or the audited algebraic, small-bias, AG, cyclic/BCH, expander, condenser, difference-set, orthogonal-array, or recent TAG templates supplies a complete campaign-admissible code of dimension greater than 1040. Within ordinary full-length Reed–Solomon concatenation with a power-of-two inner block, every proper outer-dimension-at-least-two route to `k>1040` is rigorously excluded except the hypotheses `[16384,16,8185]₂`, `[16384,17,8184]₂`, and `[16384,18,8184]₂`. The last would yield `[2^30,1170,≥535822848]₂`, but its existence remains open. This is not a global upper bound on the target dimension.
